title: HYPOTHESIS TESTING FOR QUANTIFYING LLM-HUMAN MISALIGNMENT IN MULTIPLE CHOICE SETTINGS
measurement_description: The paper proposes a hypothesis testing framework to quantify misalignment between LLM-simulated responses and human responses in multiple-choice survey settings. It specifically evaluates how well the model simulates the opinions of various demographic subgroups, including religious affiliations and religious attendance frequencies, on contentious public opinion questions.
findings: The study found that GPT-3.5-Turbo consistently failed to align with human responses across all tested demographic subgroups, including religious groups. Notably, subgroups with high religious attendance were among those least represented by the model's steered responses.
references: James Brand, Ayelet Israeli, and Donald Ngwe. Using gpt for market research, 2023.
